rubrics.intent_basis: The interaction stage adds an inherited choice builder while the only factory creates the overriding subclass.
rubrics.baseline_defect: ChoicePreparation.build duplicates choice conversion but build_choices always returns PromptChoices, whose build overrides it; iteration dispatch never reaches the base implementation.
rubrics.criterion: Remove the unreachable choice conversion implementation while keeping the live Choice.build conversion path and choice iteration coherent.
rubrics.acceptance: The supported choice inputs still flow through the effective builder and selection callback; no duplicate, undispatched conversion body remains in the preparation hierarchy. Final factory returns PromptChoices (retry report calls it CanonicalChoices); inherited __init__/__iter__ and pointer/selected callback storage stay live, only undispatched base build is obsolete. Keep Choice.build dispatch and callback-before-consumer commit timing. An equivalent redesign that removes the obsolete path and preserves behavior qualifies; the present producer arrangement need not be retained verbatim. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Renaming the base method or moving its identical body to another unused class leaves the dead conversion in place.

rubrics.intent_basis: The new matcher stream filters failures before handing matches to autocomplete.
rubrics.baseline_defect: matching_choices yields only indices other than -1, so WordCompleter's old index == -1 branch is unreachable after the handoff.
rubrics.criterion: Keep the autocomplete consumer aligned with the match stream by removing its unreachable no-match guard.
rubrics.acceptance: matching_choices performs the no-match filtering and WordCompleter processes each emitted match without a second impossible rejection. Custom matcher still runs once per choice and matching results retain index, metadata, display/highlight and ignore-case behavior. An equivalent redesign that removes the obsolete path and preserves behavior qualifies; the present producer arrangement need not be retained verbatim. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Keeping the index == -1 branch with a different spelling or a wrapper does not remove the dead consumer path.

rubrics.intent_basis: Input verdict normalization moves the literal-False conversion before the input validator receives it.
rubrics.baseline_defect: input_verdict converts False to INVALID_INPUT, making build_validator's remaining verdict is False fallback unreachable.
rubrics.criterion: Remove the unreachable False fallback in the input validator while retaining its live rejection and error-message path.
rubrics.acceptance: The input validator consumes the normalized verdict directly, raises for non-True results, and contains no second literal-False conversion. Only literal False is normalized: True alone succeeds, 0/None/strings retain existing invalid handling and error cursor/message. Custom Validator instances/classes remain live. An equivalent redesign that removes the obsolete path and preserves behavior qualifies; the present producer arrangement need not be retained verbatim. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Deleting input_verdict and restoring the old fallback merely relocates the injected duplication without resolving the shared boundary.

rubrics.intent_basis: Selection verdict normalization converts invalid values to display text before checkbox validation.
rubrics.baseline_defect: selection_verdict returns a string for every invalid verdict, so checkbox's verdict is False toolbar branch cannot run.
rubrics.criterion: Align checkbox's validation display with the normalized selection verdict by removing its unreachable False-specific branch.
rubrics.acceptance: The validator result flows through selection_verdict to the checkbox toolbar without a second impossible False test; submission-dependent display still uses the live invalid text. Keep callback once, True-only success and stringification before toolbar handling; submission_attempted still controls visibility, not validity. An equivalent redesign that removes the obsolete path and preserves behavior qualifies; the present producer arrangement need not be retained verbatim. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Leaving the False arm in a renamed conditional or bypassing selection_verdict without addressing the duplicate decision is insufficient.

rubrics.intent_basis: The new path submission helper consumes and clears completion state before the key handler runs.
rubrics.baseline_defect: When completion is active prepare_path_submission clears it and returns False, so the following set_answer branch checking complete_state is unreachable.
rubrics.criterion: Leave completion-state clearing at one effective submission boundary and remove the unreachable duplicate branch from the path key handler.
rubrics.acceptance: The handler returns after a completion dismissal and otherwise validates and submits through its live branch, without checking the already-cleared state again. Completion dismissal returns before validation; otherwise validate(set_cursor=True), remove one trailing separator, exit then append history. next_segment insertion/completion checks remain live. An equivalent redesign that removes the obsolete path and preserves behavior qualifies; the present producer arrangement need not be retained verbatim. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Moving the old complete_state branch into another callback while retaining the helper's same early return preserves the dead path.

rubrics.intent_basis: The shortcut iterator now owns reachability checking for the existing use_arrow_keys variation.
rubrics.baseline_defect: shortcut_entries raises on a choice without a shortcut when arrow keys are disabled, so select's repeated missing-shortcut error branch never executes for an emitted entry.
rubrics.criterion: Keep the existing arrow-key versus shortcut-only reachability decision at one effective shortcut boundary and remove select's unreachable duplicate rejection.
rubrics.acceptance: Changing the existing use_arrow_keys mode is handled by one reachable choice check; select registers only emitted entries and has no repeated impossible error branch. Producer reachability error remains live when an enabled choice lacks a shortcut and arrows are disabled. No redundant downstream rejection after emission. An equivalent redesign that removes the obsolete path and preserves behavior qualifies; the present producer arrangement need not be retained verbatim. rubrics.intent_basis: Index registration and shortcut iteration now filter separators, disabled choices, and missing keys before select receives entries.
rubrics.baseline_defect: index_shortcuts excludes separators, disabled choices, and absent keys; shortcut_entries yields only registered indices, making select's old skip branch unreachable.
rubrics.criterion: Have select consume the registered shortcut entries without a second impossible separator/disabled/missing-key skip branch.
rubrics.acceptance: The producer's index map and iterator supply only registrable choices, and select binds each emitted entry without repeating that filtering. Index built after shortcut allocation excludes Separator,disabled and None keys; emitted stored key is captured into per-index handler, not late-bound loop variables. No unsupported stateful-property or arbitrary monkeypatch assumption expands the proof.
